title: Telemetry-driven fallback prototypes and control-plane playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory notes and prototype ideas for a telemetry-first fallback/control-plane that can do two things: 1) reduce blast radius when a region or model pool becomes overloaded, and 2) bias traffic toward cheaper/compatible variants without violating latency SLOs. This is a working doc (ideas + sketches + TODOs).

High level goals / constraints:
- Keep user-visible latency within SLOs for tiered customers (P1-low-latency vs P2-background).
- Avoid global outages: prefer regional spillover then variant substitution then throttling.
- Keep control-plane decision loop cheap and auditable (no heavy ML in hot path).
- Use existing telemetry streams (p50/p95 queue depth, GPU util, KV cache hit rate, prefix hit ratios) as primary signals.

Key concepts (fresh nomenclature):
- Safeguard bands: GREEN / WATCH / CONSTRAIN. These are lightweight derived signals computed per region+model-family+tier.
  - GREEN: normal, allow normal routing and long-running batch windows.
  - WATCH: early-warning; surface to operators, enable short-term conservative batching and small-scale variant nudges.
  - CONSTRAIN: actively limit concurrency/batch size, prefer higher-throughput variants, enable strict fallbacks.

- Eviction policy (telemetry-driven): short-lived, targetted eviction of queued requests when KV cache pressure or queue depth predicts prolonged latency increases. Eviction favoring order: best-effort background -> lower-tier customers -> non-critical endpoints.

- Variant skewing: shifting traffic fractions across model variants (e.g., vv-large -> vv-small-fp16-quantized) based on a scoring function: score = alpha * latency_safety + beta * quality_delta + gamma * cost_savings + delta * compatibility_score. We maintain a small per-route candidate list with precomputed compatibility and regression guardrails.

Control-plane flow (sketch):
1) Telemetry ingest (metric rollups every 5s) -> precomputed derived signals (safeguard band transition).
2) Decision engine evaluates policy rules in order of precedence: safety (SLA), locality (same-region), cost guardrail, operator overrides.
3) Router config diff generated (immutable patch) with TTL and revision id. Push to edge routers (fast path) and to batch enforcers (longer TTL).
4) Router enforces decisions with soft/hard modes: soft=probabilistic skew; hard=drop/constrain/redirect.

Example scenarios:
- Scenario A: sudden spike in EU-west caused by a viral customer app. Metric triggers: p95 latency crosses 500ms, GPU util > 85%, prefix hit rate dropped 40%.
  - Transition: GREEN -> WATCH (5s) -> CONSTRAIN (after 30s sustained).
  - Actions: reduce per-request batching window in EU-west; skew 25% traffic to EU-east warm pool; move non-P1 customers to quantized variants; apply short-lived admission control on tail-heavy routes.
  - Observability: create ephemeral deck with top routes, variant switch ids, and impact estimate.

- Scenario B: a regional outage (AZ-level networking).
  - Prefer regional spillover to sibling region in same geo when latency delta < 35% and routing policy allows.
  - If sibling region capacity < required, apply variant substitution for lower-priority traffic while preserving throughput for committed customers.

Telemetry signals we care about (priority order):
- per-route p95 and p99 latency (5s rollups)
- queue depth (requests waiting for GPU scheduling)
- GPU utilization per pool
- KV cache hit ratio
- batch size distribution (actual vs target)
- prefix reuse ratio (prefix cache effectiveness)
- admission rejections / preemptions

Prototype implementation notes (low-friction):
- Use current metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> push into decision engine via short-lived aggregation service). Decision engine is a small stateless service that reads metrics and writes route diffs to configstore.
- Config diffs are versioned JSON patches (so we can audit and revert). Keep diff size minimal (fraction changes, not full configs).
- Router supports a "probabilistic override" header to allow soft experiments without global config churn.
- Fallbacks are expressed as a short list: [preferred_variant, fallback_variant_1, fallback_variant_2, admission_control]. Avoid free-form mapping in hot path.

Quality guardrails and evals:
- Each variant has a precomputed quality fingerprint per common eval set. When shifting >10% traffic to a lower-quality variant, attach an auto-rollup alert tied to the route owner.
- Quick A/B checks: send 1% of skewed traffic through a scoring pipeline (offline) for regression monitoring.

Operational playbook (short):
- WATCH band: notify on-call and create a short-lived investigation thread. No config changes unless sustained 30s.
- CONSTRAIN band: autopush config diffs described above, escalate on-call if >5min.
- Manual escape hatch: operator-run global toggle that disables all non-essential soft-skews and reverts to strict routing.

Cost heuristics: when choosing between two similar fallbacks, prefer the one that saves >X% unit cost while keeping error/latency delta within delta thresholds. X = 15% (configurable per customer tier).

Open questions / risks (TODO):
- How to represent progressive degradation in customer billing logs and explainable incidents to customers (transparency vs signal noise).
- Edge cases where variant substitution breaks deterministic outputs (embeddings drift, reranking). Need per-route opt-out metadata.
- Frequency of telemetry -> decisions: 5s vs 15s vs 60s tradeoffs. Faster reacts but increases config churn.
- How to safely test control-plane changes in canary mode without causing oscillation. Consider hysteresis and minimum hold times.

Mini backlog / next steps:
- [P0] Prototype decision engine that reads Prometheus summaries and writes a config diff to a test router (owner: Miguel). (2w)
- [P1] Implement probabilistic override header and router-side support for soft-skew (owner: Sophie). (3w)
- [P1] Build small quality fingerprint store per variant and integrate regression alert on >10% traffic shift (owner: Priya). (2w)
- [P2] Draft customers-facing incident messaging for graceful degradation events (owner: David). (1w)
- [P3] Run chaos test (partial region throttle) in staging to validate spillover choreography. (Q1 next cycle)
Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the decision engine deterministic for a given input snapshot to make debugging reproducible.
- Avoid "continuous learning" in hot path; if ML used, run offline and push thresholds/config.
- Watch the pacing of automatic reverts; add local backoffs to prevent oscillation when sibling region recovers intermittently.

References and inspiration:
- Prior work: regional-pricing-and-hedging notes (internal), but this intentionally focuses on telemetry+control-plane rather than pure route math.
- Related tickets: ENG-1329 (decision-engine epics), OPS-217 (observability dashboards for safeguard bands).

If this looks reasonable I'll: 1) spin up a tiny PoC repo and wire the metric consumer -> configstore path, 2) do a tabletop with SRE and product to validate guardrails.

End of doc.
